title: Interventional, open-label, extension trial of asedebart (Lu AG13909) in participants with congenital adrenal hyperplasia
official: Interventional, open-label, extension trial of asedebart (Lu AG13909) in participants with congenital adrenal hyperplasia
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the safety and tolerability of long-term treatment with asedebart in participants with classic CAH
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. The participant has previously been treated with asedebart in a CAH trial.
2. 2. The participant had an acceptable benefit-risk in the previous trial and would benefit from continued asedebart treatment.
3. 3. The participant takes a daily dose of GC replacement therapy of xxxxx (adjusted for body surface area in HCe) at the start of the trial.
4. 4. Are willing and able to attend all required study visits
5. 5. Can read and understand the study information and provide written informed consent.
6. 6. Women who can become pregnant must have a negative pregnancy test before joining the study. They must also either be unable to become pregnant, have a partner who has been permanently sterilized, or agree to use an highly effective method of contraception during the study and for approximately 4.5 months after the last dose of asedebart. In addition, they must not donate eggs during this period.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. The participant is a member of the site staff or of their immediate families or is a subordinate (or immediate family member of a subordinate) to any of the site staff.
2. 11. The participant is currently or has recently (< 3 months prior to screening) been taking any immunosuppressive treatment (except for their GC replacement therapy).
3. 12. The participant has had a significant blood loss < 3 months prior to the first dose of asedebart in this trial (e.g., surgery, trauma, blood donation)
4. 13. The participant has had major surgery (excluding uncomplicated laparoscopic procedures, e.g., cholecystectomy/appendectomy) < 6 months prior to the first dose of asedebart in this trial.
5. 14. The participant has, at the Screening/Baseline Visit: an abnormal ECG that is considered clinically significant by the investigator as calculated by the ECG equipment and evaluated by the investigator, a PR interval >200 ms, a QRS interval >110 ms, a QTcF interval >450 ms (based on the Fridericia correction where QTcF = QT/RR0.33), an out-of-range or abnormal ECG may be repeated once.
6. 2. The participant has known hyper-sensitivity or intolerance to asedebart or its excipients.
7. 3. The participant has taken any IMP other than asedebart < 3 months or < 5 half lives, whichever is longer, prior to the first dose of asedebart in this trial.
8. 4. The participant is pregnant, breastfeeding, intends to become pregnant, or is of childbearing potential and not willing to use adequate contraceptive methods.
9. 5. The participant has an increased risk of adrenal crisis in the opinion of the investigator (for example history of repeated adrenal crisis in recent years, history of adrenal crisis caused by reduction of GC dose).
10. 6. The participant has a current diagnosis or history of substance abuse or alcohol abuse (DSM5® criteria)
11. 7. The participant has a condition that requires regular or long-term treatment with any systemic steroid medication for other reasons than replacement therapy due to CAH.
12. 8. The participant has a disease or takes medication that could, in the opinion of the investigator, interfere with the assessments of safety, tolerability, efficacy, or interfere with the conduct or interpretation of the trial.
13. 9. The participant has a clinically significant abnormal ECG parameter, vital signs value, or other safety findings at the screening visit that indicate a potential risk for the participant if enrolled, in the opinion of the investigator.
14. 10. The participant is, in the opinion of the investigator, unlikely to comply with the Clinical Trial Protocol or is unsuitable for any reason.
